PHYSICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #1
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: PHYSICS
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Glucose and oxygen

2. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Pressure? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Pressure.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Pressure.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Pressure.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Pressure.

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes.

5. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 37 °C

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Current Electricity Measurement of current, e.m.f., potential difference and res? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Current Electricity Measurement of current, e.m.f., potential difference and res.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Current Electricity Measurement of current, e.m.f., potential difference and res.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Current Electricity Measurement of current, e.m.f., potential difference and res.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Current Electricity Measurement of current, e.m.f., potential difference and res.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Physics? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Physics.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Physics.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Physics.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Physics.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Moments and equilibrium? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Moments and equilibrium.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Moments and equilibrium.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Moments and equilibrium.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Moments and equilibrium.

9. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Milk souring
   D. Iron rusting

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Properties of Waves? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Properties of Waves.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Properties of Waves.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Properties of Waves.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Waves.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Mechanical Properties of Materials? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Mechanical Properties of Materials.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Mechanical Properties of Materials.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mechanical Properties of Materials.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Mechanical Properties of Materials.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Energy, Work, Power and Machines? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Energy, Work, Power and Machines.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Energy, Work, Power and Machines.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Energy, Work, Power and Machines.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Energy, Work, Power and Machines.

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Electronics? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Electronics.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Electronics.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Electronics.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Electronics.

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change 4.2 Introduction to Space Physics Page 15 o? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change 4.2 Introduction to Space Physics Page 15 o.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change 4.2 Introduction to Space Physics Page 15 o.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change 4.2 Introduction to Space Physics Page 15 o.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change 4.2 Introduction to Space Physics Page 15 o.

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change.

16. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Removing all vegetation

17. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. watt (W)
   D. joule (J)

18. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Producers

19. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

20. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

21. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. Heating until a solid melts

22. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Temperature and Thermal Expansion? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Temperature and Thermal Expansion.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Temperature and Thermal Expansion.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Temperature and Thermal Expansion.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Temperature and Thermal Expansion.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
23. In three clear sentences, explain Temperature and Thermal Expansion and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Moments and equilibrium and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Energy, Work, Power and Machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

26. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of Waves and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

27. In three clear sentences, explain Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

28. In three clear sentences, explain Current Electricity Measurement of current, e.m.f., potential difference and res and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

29. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Electronics and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

30. In three clear sentences, explain Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change 4.2 Introduction to Space Physics Page 15 o and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

31. In three clear sentences, explain Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

32. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Space Physics Page 15 of 62 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL P and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
